title: Profile
description: <.jad>/profiles/<category>/<name>.json. The profile name is the file name. A profile picks a prompt, the models it may use, one toolset or a list of toolsets and setting overrides.

name.description: Display name of the profile, shown beside its ID in lists and the profile picker. Defaults to the profile ID.

instructions.description: System-prompt text placed before the prompt documents, in the prompt_role. It is the profile's, so every model the profile offers gets it. A model file may not carry instructions.

models.description: Narrows the models. Items: "<category>" for a whole folder, "<category>/<name>" for one file, or "*". A missing key offers every model; [] offers none. An item that matches no model is a load error.

model_default.description: Model used when a request names none, written <category>/<name> with an optional @<effort>, for example "openai/gpt-deep" or "openai/gpt-deep@high". The model must be one of the profile's models (which list plain IDs); the effort must be listed in the model file's efforts. The effort applies only while the run uses this model and no @effort of its own; it overrides the model file's default_effort. Without model_default, the first model (by ID) is used.

toolset.description: The toolset this profile uses, or a list of them, each written <category>/<name> under tools/, for example "coding/full". Any toolset may be used. Given a list, the toolsets merge in order: when two name the same native tool or MCP server the first listed wins, with a warning, and only the first toolset with hooks supplies hooks (a later one's hooks are ignored with a warning). Without it the profile has no native tool and no MCP tool.

tools.description: Which registered tools the profile's model sees. allow lists them, deny takes some away and wins over allow; without allow every registered tool is shown except what deny names. deny also limits the profile's sub-agents: a tool it covers is in no agent's catalog, and an agent that lists only denied tools fails to load. A tool left out is hidden from the profile's model only; a sub-agent can still use it when its agent lists it. Each entry is a native tool name, mcp:<server>:<tool> or mcp:<server>:*. An entry that names a tool the session does not register is a configuration error. An empty allow array hides every registered tool; hosted tools from the model file (such as web search) are not registered tools and stay.

allow.description: Tools the model sees, as the names of a tool or an mcp:<server>:<tool> entry. tools.lazy entries, and load_tool while tools.lazy is non-empty, count as allowed and need not be repeated here. A tool_smith script can call only the tools this shows.

deny.description: Tools the model does not see, as the names of a tool or an mcp:<server>:<tool> entry; wins over allow. A tool_smith script cannot call them either.

lazy.description: Tools the model sees by name and one-line summary only, through load_tool: it lists them, describes them (full description and inputSchema) and runs one with run and arguments. A lazy tool is never in the tools array, and a call that names it directly is refused with lazy_tool_not_loaded and a pointer to load_tool run. Only MCP tools (mcp:<server>:<tool> or mcp:<server>:*) and extension tools (decide_systemone, web_search) can be lazy: a native tool (skill, subagent, task, exec, read_image, records, load_tool and the others) is always in the tools array and is refused as a lazy entry at load, with an error naming the entry; load_tool cannot be lazy either. A lazy entry counts as allowed, so it need not be repeated in allow (a whole-server entry "mcp:<server>:*" only while allow names nothing of that server: otherwise allow decides which of its tools are shown, and the wildcard makes them lazy), and while the list is non-empty load_tool counts as allowed too; deny still wins, and a lazy entry that deny covers, or a deny that names load_tool, is a configuration error. Needs tools.native.load_tool, or the profile is refused at load. A sub-agent, a nested subagent or profile_message child gets its owner's lazy tools gated with the same set (its load_tool dispatches through its own catalog), and load_tool only when the owner enables it and the agent lists it.

lazy_summary_bytes.description: Largest size of the one-line summary the model sees for each lazy tool, cut at a character boundary. The full description and inputSchema are returned by load_tool names.

lazy_load_max.description: Most lazy tools one load_tool describe call (names) may match; a longer batch is refused and nothing is described.

settings.description: Overrides of the setting keys listed in propertyNames. Objects merge key by key with the level above; arrays and scalars replace it. Each value follows the same key in setting.schema.json.
